text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Monetary Fund has agreed to support the second phase of Zimbabwe's economic reforms, reversing its decision last year to halt balance of payments support worth Z$1 billion after the government missed key economic targets set by the institution, Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa said on Wednesday.
- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe said on Wednesday it had lowered its key rediscount rate to 27 percent from 27.5 percent, citing a decline in annual inflation.

- Some Zimbabwean textile companies have become impatient with South Africa's reluctance to implement a recently agreed preferential deal and have stopped exporting to that country, industry sources said this week.

- Southern African businesses should look more to the region if they are serious about creating a trading bloc that can challenge any other in the world and thereby benefit the over 135 million people in the region, a Harare businessman said this week.

- Economic relations between Zimbabwe and Yugoslavia are set to be strengthened with the expected signing of at least three major cooperation agreements between the two countries during the four-day state visit by Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic.
